title: Network Types (LAN, WAN, MAN, PAN, WLAN, SAN, VPN)
source: 02. Network Types (LAN, WAN, MAN, PAN, WLAN, SAN, VPN).md

cards.a: By geographic scope (PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN), by transmission medium (WLAN, SAN), or by who controls them and how connectivity is provided (VPN). A single enterprise typically uses all of these at once.

cards.q: What is a PAN and what are examples?
cards.a: A Personal Area Network, spanning about 1 to 10 meters for one person. Examples include Bluetooth, USB, Infrared, and UWB.

cards.q: What is a LAN and what technology dominates it?
cards.a: A Local Area Network spanning a building or campus with high speed and low latency. Switched Ethernet is the dominant LAN technology, and it uses owner-operated, high-bandwidth (Gbps) equipment.

cards.q: What is a MAN and what are typical technologies?
cards.a: A Metropolitan Area Network spanning a city (kilometers to tens of kilometers). Typical technologies include city fiber rings and Metro Ethernet, placing it between LAN and WAN.

cards.q: What is a WAN and what technologies are used?
cards.a: A Wide Area Network spanning intercity or global distances, typically carrier-provided. Technologies include MPLS, dedicated circuits (T1/E1, dark fiber), broadband (DSL/cable), cellular (LTE/5G), and modern SD-WAN overlays.

cards.q: What are the characteristics of a WAN compared to a LAN?
cards.a: A WAN is leased from service providers, with lower per-unit bandwidth, higher latency, and more cost, and its operation is governed by an SLA covering availability, delay, jitter, and loss.

cards.q: What is a WLAN and what standard does it use?
cards.a: A Wireless LAN that uses radio waves (RF) instead of cabling, based on the IEEE 802.11 family with standard Wi-Fi on 2.4, 5, and 6 GHz bands. It is managed by access points and Wireless LAN Controllers (WLC).

cards.q: How does a WLAN compare to a wired LAN?
cards.a: A WLAN offers more convenience and mobility but suffers more RF interference, uses a shared medium, and has greater security exposure compared to wired LAN.

cards.q: What is a SAN and what technologies does it use?
cards.a: A Storage Area Network, a dedicated high-speed network connecting servers to block-level storage arrays. It often uses Fibre Channel (a dedicated fabric) or iSCSI/FCoE over Ethernet, and is optimized for throughput, low latency, and reliability.

cards.q: What is the difference between SAN and NAS?
cards.a: SAN is block-level storage over a dedicated network (Fibre Channel or iSCSI), while NAS is file-level storage over the regular LAN/IP. NAS is a related concept to SAN.

cards.q: What is a VPN and what does it provide?
cards.a: A VPN is a logical, encrypted tunnel over an existing network (often the Internet or MPLS). It provides confidentiality (encryption), integrity, authentication, and a private addressing overlay without owning physical links.

cards.q: What are the two types of VPN and examples of each?
cards.a: Site-to-site, which connects two branch/office networks (using IPsec or DMVPN), and remote access, which connects an individual user or device to the enterprise (using SSL/IPsec VPN).

cards.q: How does cost and control change as network geographic scope grows?
cards.a: Cost increases in the order PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN; speed and latency degrade as scope grows; and control decreases as scope grows because the carrier owns the WAN.

cards.q: Why is 'the Internet is a WAN' an incorrect statement?
cards.a: The Internet is a network of networks; a WAN is one type of network. The Internet is not itself a WAN, though an ISP's backbone is a WAN example.

cards.q: Is a VPN for two buildings in the same city still a VPN regardless of distance?
cards.a: Yes. Scope and ownership are separate axes, so a VPN connecting two buildings in the same city is still a VPN regardless of distance.

cards.q: Why is a WLAN not considered a separate topology?
cards.a: The WLAN is not a separate topology; it is a transmission classification based on using radio waves (RF) rather than cabling.

cards.q: On a Cisco switch, what commands create VLAN 10 named Users?
cards.a: Enter vlan 10 under global config, then name Users: switch(config)# vlan 10, switch(config-vlan)# name Users.

cards.q: What is the trade-off a VPN makes compared to dedicated WAN circuits?
cards.a: A VPN trades some performance for privacy and lower cost compared to dedicated WAN circuits.
